glossUnihan: words, speech; speak, say; Kangxi radical 149
form: Mojidata IDS: 亠 + 二 + 口
formNote: The Shuowen: 直言曰言，論難曰語 — “speaking directly is 言; disputing is 語.” As a component it becomes 訁, the radical of words and speaking (as in 信, 語, 說).
summary: Speech, words, to say: the radical of every word about words. The Daodejing distrusts it (知者不言), Confucius builds order on it (名不正，則言不順), and the Chinese Bible nearly chose it for the Logos.
placement: At the very top of the band, on its far side, above 實: speech at the summit. (Placement is a design choice, not a claim.)

oc.note: † Baracus, from general knowledge; not yet checked against B–S 2014.

satellites.title: Those Who Know Do Not Speak
satellites.evidence: Daodejing ch. 56: 知者不言，言者不知 — “those who know do not speak; those who speak do not know.” A text of five thousand characters that distrusts words: the tension is part of the book.

satellites.title: Direct Speech, and Dispute
satellites.evidence: The Shuowen separates two words for speaking: 直言曰言，論難曰語 — 言 is saying a thing straight, 語 is answering and arguing. The plain statement and the exchange are different acts.
